title: Activation lifecycle for customer region requests
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define a repeatable, time-boxed activation lifecycle that turns a validated customer region/residency request into a production-capable region (or failover entitlement) with clear handoffs between Sales/CS, PM, Eng, Infra, and Legal. This ticket captures the end-to-end checklist, SLAs for each stage, risk trade-offs, and a lightweight communication plan so customers see predictable timelines for region enablement.
background: We receive ad-hoc region/residency requests from enterprise customers that range from the need for a new geo region to strict data residency contracts. Current intake focuses on prioritization; customers frequently ask for predictable timelines and clearer status. This lifecycle standardizes the work from intake -> technical validation -> procurement & compliance -> capacity provisioning -> rollout -> verification -> handback to CS.
goals: (1) Reduce average time-to-activation for high-priority residency requests to <= 6 weeks for greenfield cloud regions and <= 12 weeks for on-prem/residency exceptions; (2) Provide a standardized customer-facing timeline and weekly status cadence; (3) Ensure all activations have documented SLOs, rollback criteria, and security sign-off.
out_of_scope: Changes to pricing model for dedicated capacity, implementation of new internal billing systems, or building new long-term data-center partnerships. Those will be separate initiatives.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A published activation checklist in Confluence with explicit owner for each step; 2) An intake -> activation Kanban template added to Linear for tracking; 3) Two pilot activations run end-to-end with CS and customer feedback recorded; 4) Playbook includes cost estimate template and required artifacts for legal/compliance sign-off.
milestones: Intake rubric finalization (2026-02-25) -> Technical feasibility gate (2026-03-05) -> Compliance sign-off template (2026-03-12) -> Capacity provisioning runbook (2026-03-20) -> Pilot activation 1 (2026-03-28) -> Pilot activation 2 and retrospective (2026-03-31)
intake_flow_summary: 1) Customer submits residency request via intake form -> 2) Triage scoring (legal sensitivity, revenue, strategic) -> 3) Assign activation owner -> 4) Technical feasibility assessment -> 5) Cost + capacity estimate -> 6) Compliance & contract pathing -> 7) Provisioning -> 8) Rollout & verification -> 9) Handoff to CS.
technical_feasibility_checks: Model compatibility (quantization/latency targets), data path isolation (VPC subnets, KMS keys), dependency on partner regions, required HA/failover topology, and estimated GPU footprint. Include checklist items and required sign-offs from ENG/Infra.
cost_and_capacity_playbook: Template for capacity estimate (steady qps, peak qps, batching), estimated monthly cost with sensitivity band, options for Dedicated vs. Hosted workaround, and recommended autoscaling thresholds. Guidance for offering short-term credits or migration assistance.
compliance_and_contracting_pathways: Decision tree: standard clause -> include residency addendum -> require on-prem/private deployment -> require data processing agreement update. Attach example contract snippets and link to Legal ticket template. Note regulatory jurisdictions that need additional checks (APAC finance, EU health data).
rollout_strategy: Canary rollouts across a small set of customer requests, automated traffic shaping with metrics thresholds (latency, error-rate, cost per token), pre-defined rollback triggers, and post-activation audit (logs, KMS access review). Include blackout windows and maintenance windows coordination.
communication_plan: Customer-facing timeline with stage gates and expected SLAs, weekly status email templates, and a public-facing support doc for expected behaviors during activation. CS will provide a single point-of-contact and patch notes for the customer.
risk_tradeoffs: Faster activation reduces sales friction but increases operational risk if capacity planning is optimistic. Trade-offs: (a) Accept higher cost (reserved capacity) vs. slower timeline, (b) Offer a limited feature set in new region to shorten time-to-value, (c) Use hosted fallback routes vs. full private deployment.
decision_log: 2026-02-20: Agreed to time-box technical feasibility to 5 business days (Asha, Priya). 2026-02-27: For high-revenue customers, permit temporary cross-region routing under NDA while private VPC is provisioned (Legal approved). 2026-03-02: Require security review for any region with on-prem or HSM involvement (Claire Meyer).
open_questions: 1) How to price short-term cross-region fallbacks? 2) What is the SLA compensation model for multi-week provisioning misses? 3) Who owns multi-cloud interconnect procurement if customer requires carrier cross-connects?
pilot_plan: Select two queued enterprise requests: (a) EU region for payments company (high compliance sensitivity), (b) APAC region for media customer (high throughput). Run full lifecycle and collect timing, blockers, and customer satisfaction score.
success_metrics: Median time-to-activation (days), pilot CSAT, # of rollbacks within 30 days, accuracy of capacity estimate (within 20%), and number of activations completed without security exceptions.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Create Linear template for activation lifecycle (PM owner). 2) Add automated intake fields to capture compliance artifacts. 3) Schedule runbook walkthrough with Eng/Infra. 4) Draft customer-facing timeline and FAQ.
recent_updates: 2026-02-19: Draft checklist posted to Confluence for initial review. 2026-02-24: Eng added feasibility gating template and asked for additional telemetry requirements. 2026-03-03: Legal provided residency addendum examples. 2026-03-10: Pilot customer A confirmed readiness window; provisioning slot requested with Infra.
notes_for_engineering: Eng to provide a minimal viable provisioning script for greenfield regions that automates VPC/subnet setup, model deployment, and canary traffic config. Instrument endpoints for cost & latency telemetry per activation.
notes_for_sales_cs: Template emails and SLA language to be provided to Sales; CS should get training on status categories and escalation path. For high-risk customers, recommend a kickoff call with Infra within 48 hours of feasibility sign-off.
retrospective_plan: After two pilots, run a 90-minute retrospective with Eng, PM, Infra, CS, Legal. Capture time deltas per stage and update the checklist. Publish a short change log and update customer-facing timeline.
